title: Checking into a hotel
situation: You arrive at a hotel front desk to check in for your stay.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello. I would like to check in.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, do you have a reservation?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I booked online.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What is your name?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It is Kim Minsu. I booked two nights.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please show me your passport.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Here it is. Is breakfast included too?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 네, 칠 층 식당에서 드시면 돼요.
lines.en: Yes, you can eat at the restaurant on the seventh floor.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. What is the room number?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 삼백오 호예요. 카드 키 여기 있어요.
lines.en: It is room 305. Here is your card key.

tip: Korean hotels usually ask for your passport at check-in, so keep it handy.

title: Meeting someone new
situation: You meet a new coworker for the first time and introduce yourself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Hello. Nice to meet you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Hello. Glad to meet you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: I am Sarah. I came from America.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Oh, really? I am Jihun.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Nice to meet you. What work do you do?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: I am a designer. How about you, Sarah?

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: I am an English teacher.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Wow, that is cool. You speak Korean well.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Not at all. I still speak only a little.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: I look forward to working with you.

tip: Koreans add the title 씨 after a given name to be polite, but never use it for yourself.

title: A short call to a friend
situation: You call a friend to make plans to meet later today.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Hello? Jimin, it is me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Oh, hi! What are you doing now?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ko: 그냥 집에 있어. 오늘 시간 있어?
lines.en: Just staying home. Do you have time today?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Yeah, the evening is fine. Why?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ko: 같이 영화 볼래? 새 영화 나왔어.
lines.en: Want to watch a movie together? A new one came out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Sounds good! What time should we meet?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ko: 여섯 시 어때? 역 앞에서 보자.
lines.en: How about six? Let us meet in front of the station.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Got it. See you later then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Okay, do not be late. I will hang up!

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Okay, see you later. Bye!

tip: Always answer the phone in Korean with 여보세요, even if you already know who is calling.
